newsitem.title: POLAND: Stalexport says big interest in bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Stalexport says big interest in bond issue.

text.p: Twenty-five foreign investment banks have expressed interest in joining lead manager Robert Fleming to underwrite the convertible bond issue of Polish steel trader Stalexport SA, Stalexport's spokesman said.

"There's been a lot of interest...25 banks have shown interest in servicing the issue, which shows they're convinced the issue will sell well" Jacek Czeladko told Reuters on Wednesday, adding that the firm sought to complete the issue by late March or early April.
Czeladko said that so far the London-based capital-market units of Lazard Brothers, Salomon Brothers and Nomura had agreed to underwrite the bonds but he would not say how many.
Stalexport plans to issue 50,000 five-to-seven-year convertible eurobonds at a par value of $1,000.
Czeladko said the firm seeks a listing for the bonds on the London or Luxembourg bourse, preferably the former.
Stalexport shareholders have already approved the bonds and a four-million-share issue for which they could be exchanged.
Czeladko said the bonds would be directed to foreign and Polish institutional investors, but that the latter would need to apply for permission to buy them using foreign currency.
In December the firm's president said state-owned Bank Pekao SA, Polish Development Bank (PBR) and BIG were interested in the bonds and that management would also offer them to BPH and BRE.
Stalexport's management will determine the bonds' conversion date and interest, which will not be higher than five percent of the bond's nominal value annually.
The bonds will be exchangeable for shares six months after the issue at the earliest.
The shares would be converted at the average price of the shares during three sessions before the issue plus a premium of at least 15 percent in dollar terms.
Stalexport also said the bonds would be callable after three years at par value plus a coupon equal to the interest on comparable five or seven year U.S. treasury bonds plus 125-175 basis points.
